accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Wildlife Institute of India — Dehradun
2. Botanical Survey of India — Kolkata
3. Forest Survey of India — Lucknow
4. G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment — Kosi-Katarmal, Almora
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The Wildlife Institute of India is at Dehradun, the Botanical Survey of India is at Kolkata and GBPNIHE is at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora. The Forest Survey of India is also at Dehradun, not Lucknow.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong location by comparing institutes that are commonly associated with Dehradun and Kolkata.
accepted.sec: Environmental research institutes → location

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institute)
a. Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History
b. Indian Institute of Toxicology Research
c. Central Marine Living Resources and Ecology

d. Zoological Survey of India

List-II (Location)
i. Kochi
ii. Coimbatore
iii. Lucknow
iv. Kolkata

Choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv
a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i
a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i
a–iv, b–iii, c–ii, d–i
accepted.x: SACON is located at Coimbatore, IITR at Lucknow, CMLRE at Kochi and ZSI at Kolkata.

accepted.s: The Forest Survey of India was established in which year?
accepted.x: The Forest Survey of India was established in 1981 and is located at Dehradun.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the establishment year from the years associated with other environmental bodies.

accepted.s: The Central Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE) is associated with which of the following?
o: A Himalayan environment institute at Almora
A toxicology research institute at Lucknow
A national deep-sea fauna repository named “Bhavasagara” at Kochi
A bird research centre at Coimbatore
accepted.x: CMLRE is associated with the “Bhavasagara” national deep-sea fauna repository at Kochi.
accepted.tq: Link the specialised function and distinctive name with the correct institute and location.
accepted.sec: Environmental research institutes → location

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Wildlife Institute of India is correct?
o: It is located at Kolkata and administers the NBA Fund.
It is located at Dehradun and monitors NR7 targets.
It is located at Kochi and monitors NR7 targets.
It is located at Almora and implements Namami Gange.
accepted.x: The Wildlife Institute of India is located at Dehradun and is associated with monitoring NR7 targets.
accepted.tq: Combine the institution’s location with its specific current monitoring role.
accepted.sec: Environmental research institutes → location

accepted.s: The Environmental Information System (ENVIS), now known as EIACP, is best described as:
o: A network of environmental-information centres of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
A statutory tribunal for environmental disputes
A pollution-abatement programme for rivers outside the Ganga basin
A biodiversity approval mechanism for foreign companies
accepted.x: ENVIS is the MoEFCC’s network of environmental-information centres and is now known as EIACP.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional network by matching its function with the responsible ministry.
accepted.sec: Environmental research institutes → location

accepted.s: The National Biodiversity Authority is headquartered at:
o: Chennai
Bengaluru
New Delhi
Hyderabad
accepted.x: The headquarters of the National Biodiversity Authority is at Chennai.
accepted.tq: Test the headquarters directly while using nearby environmental institutions as distractors.
accepted.sec: National Biodiversity Authority - HQ, year, biopiracy, three tiers, APSBB

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-tier institutional structure under biodiversity governance?
o: SBBs at the national level, NBA at the State level and BMCs at the district level
NBA at the national level, SBBs at the State level and BMCs at the local level
NBA at the local level, BMCs at the State level and SBBs at the national level
BMCs at the national level, SBBs at the local level and NBA at the State level
accepted.x: The three tiers are the National Biodiversity Authority at the national level, State Biodiversity Boards at the State level and Biodiversity Management Committees at the local level.
accepted.tq: Arrange the bodies by jurisdiction from national to local.
accepted.sec: National Biodiversity Authority - HQ, year, biopiracy, three tiers, APSBB

accepted.s: With reference to biopiracy, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Foreigners may access Indian bio-resources without approval if no patent is sought.
Foreigners require approval of the NBA to access bio-resources or traditional knowledge, and NBA approval precedes intellectual property rights on them.
Only local bodies can grant approval for foreign access to traditional knowledge.
NBA approval is required only after intellectual property rights have been granted.
accepted.x: Foreigners require NBA approval to access bio-resources or associated traditional knowledge, and such approval precedes the grant of intellectual property rights. Access and benefit-sharing with local communities is also an important safeguard.
accepted.tq: Apply the approval-sequence rule and reject options that reverse the order or shift authority.
accepted.sec: National Biodiversity Authority - HQ, year, biopiracy, three tiers, APSBB

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an initiative associated with the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board?
o: Implementation of the Namami Gange programme throughout Andhra Pradesh
Biodiversity parks on the flood plains of five polluted rivers
Pilot cultivation of Gloriosa superba
City Biodiversity Index in Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Kadapa and Tirupati
accepted.x: The City Biodiversity Index, biodiversity parks on the flood plains of five polluted rivers and the Gloriosa superba cultivation pilot are APSBB initiatives. Namami Gange is implemented by the NMCG.
accepted.tq: Find the option belonging to another environmental body rather than the APSBB.
accepted.sec: National Biodiversity Authority - HQ, year, biopiracy, three tiers, APSBB

accepted.s: The National Biodiversity Authority Act was amended in 2023 and the Biological Diversity Rules were issued in:
accepted.x: The Biological Diversity Rules were issued in 2024, following the amendment of the Act in 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of the Act amendment from the year of the Rules.
accepted.sec: National Biodiversity Authority - HQ, year, biopiracy, three tiers, APSBB

accepted.s: Which one of the following bodies replaced the Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority (EPCA) in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas?
o: National Mission for Clean Ganga
Commission for Air Quality Management
National Biodiversity Authority
Central Ground Water Authority
accepted.x: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), established under the CAQM Act, 2021, replaced EPCA in the NCR and adjoining areas.
accepted.tq: Use the replacement relationship and distinguish air-quality authority from water and biodiversity bodies.
accepted.sec: Other statutory bodies - CAQM, CGWA, NMCG

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CAQM Act was enacted in 2021.
2. CAQM covers the National Capital Region and adjoining areas.
3. CAQM replaced the EPCA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. CAQM operates in the NCR and adjoining areas under the CAQM Act, 2021, replacing EPCA.
accepted.tq: Verify the body through its legal basis, territorial scope and predecessor.
accepted.sec: Other statutory bodies - CAQM, CGWA, NMCG

accepted.s: The National Mission for Clean Ganga is the successor set-up to which body?
o: NGRBA
CGWA
EPCA
NBA
accepted.x: NMCG is the successor set-up to the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA), which was established in 2009 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
accepted.tq: Use the predecessor–successor relationship and distinguish river-basin institutions from pollution authorities.
accepted.sec: Other statutory bodies - CAQM, CGWA, NMCG

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the principal implementation role of the National Mission for Clean Ganga?
o: Implementing Namami Gange
Monitoring NR7 targets in wildlife institutions
Preparing City Biodiversity Indices
Regulating access to traditional knowledge by foreigners
accepted.x: The NMCG implements the Namami Gange programme.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme directly associated with the body’s mandate.

38 rivers in 16 States outside the Ganga basin
16 rivers in 38 States outside the Ganga basin
38 rivers in all States within the Ganga basin

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the criticism concerning the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
o: It has no statutory or administrative role in environmental information systems.
It is criticised only for transferring all functions to State governments.
It is criticised as overfunded and excessively centralised in implementation.
It is criticised as underfunded and siloed.
accepted.x: A stated criticism is that MoEFCC is underfunded and operates in silos.
accepted.tq: Select the precise criticism and avoid reversing the paired descriptors.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the oldest national pollution body and the institution that replaced the NEAA?
o: NGT, established in 1974; CPCB, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1981; CAQM, established in 2010
CGWA, established in 1974; NMCG, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1974; NGT, established in 2010
accepted.x: CPCB, established in 1974, is the oldest national pollution body. The NGT, established in 2010, replaced the National Environment Appellate Authority (NEAA).
accepted.tq: Pair the correct institution with its year and distinguish the pollution regulator from the appellate tribunal.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: NMCG — Namami Gange
CAQM — CAQM Act, 2021
CGWA — Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act
NBA — National Clean Air Programme
accepted.x: NBA is associated with biodiversity governance, not the National Clean Air Programme. CAQM, CGWA and NMCG are correctly matched with their respective legal basis or programme.
accepted.tq: Find the body–function mismatch by separating biodiversity, air-quality, groundwater and river missions.
accepted.sec: Other statutory bodies - CAQM, CGWA, NMCG

accepted.s: A foreign company seeks to use a traditional medicinal practice of an Indian local community for developing a commercial product. Which institutional requirement is most appropriate?
o: It requires approval only after obtaining intellectual property rights.
It may proceed without approval because traditional knowledge is not a bio-resource.
It requires approval only from the NMCG.
It must obtain NBA approval, with access and benefit-sharing involving local communities.
accepted.x: Foreign access to bio-resources or associated traditional knowledge requires NBA approval, and benefit-sharing with local communities is part of the framework. NBA approval precedes intellectual property rights on such resources or knowledge.
accepted.tq: Apply the biopiracy safeguards to a realistic access-and-commercialisation situation.
